emergency.condition_text: the colours have stopped arriving, or a land-hate effect has taken them
indications: Four or five lands on turn six while the table is on eight or more
A hand of six-drops and one cost reducer, with nothing castable this turn
Blood Moon or an equivalent resolved: eight basics survive it — four Mountain, two Forest, one Island, one Plains — and there is no Swamp in the 99
Black is the colour that strands first: 18 sources against a 30-source target (audit, colour-sources)
Two of the mana sources in play are Delighted Halfling and Cavern of Souls, and the spell in hand is not legendary and not a Dragon
immediate: Play the land that makes the colour you are missing, not the one that enters untapped. Battlefield Forge, City of Brass, Mana Confluence, Shivan Reef, Spire of Industry and Tarnished Citadel all enter untapped and all charge life; pay it.

Cast Bloom Tender or Faeburrow Elder ahead of any other two-mana play. Both add one mana per colour already among your permanents, and Bloom Tender on turn two is what made the mana work in the game logged as 003.
Point Farseek at Blood Crypt, Overgrown Tomb or Smoldering Marsh. Farseek is the only tutor in the deck that fetches a Swamp type, and black is the short colour.

Cast the cost reducer before the ramp spell when you can only have one. Eminence is already taking {1} off every other Dragon from the command zone; Dragonspeaker Shaman or Urza's Incubator takes {2} more.
Stop tapping Forbidden Orchard for colour once an opponent has a fight effect or a sacrifice outlet. Each tap hands a named opponent a 1/1.
subsequent: Under a land-hate lock, play the red half of the deck and pick one seat. Glorybringer, Smaug the Magnificent and Terror of the Peaks are castable off Mountains alone; Crux of Fate, Swords to Plowshares, Teferi's Protection and Flawless Maneuver are not.

Cast Skyshroud Claim off five mana rather than a five-drop Dragon. It puts two Forest-typed lands in untapped, and Breeding Pool, Canopy Vista, Cinder Glade, Overgrown Tomb and Stomping Ground all carry the type.
Recast The Ur-Dragon only once a printed reducer is on the battlefield. Urza's Incubator and Dragonspeaker Shaman together take it from nine mana to five.
Hold Chromatic Lantern for the turn a colour is actually missing rather than casting it on curve; it turns every land you control into a source of that colour.
emergency.notes: Six of this deck's mana sources are restricted and cannot pay for a spell that is not a Dragon or a legend: Cavern of Souls, Unclaimed Territory, Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon, Delighted Halfling, Sarkhan, Fireblood and Desolation of Smaug. None of them can pay for Crux of Fate, Swords to Plowshares, Heroic Intervention, or an equip cost. Count that mana twice before you decide a hand is castable — deck-facts warns on exactly this.

emergency.condition_text: the table is answering your pieces one at a time
indications: Your only cost reducer is on the battlefield and the second is in hand
Gadrak, the Crown-Scourge on the battlefield with fewer than four artifacts — he cannot attack, and the table can count the artifacts he needs
An opponent passing with two or more untapped sources and no board action for a turn cycle
Lightning Greaves in play attached to nothing
Smaug the Magnificent attacking for a number equal to your Treasures, and the Treasures are the removable half
immediate: Name the piece the table is answering. If it is a cost reducer, leave the second one in hand until the first is gone.
Equip Lightning Greaves in your main phase, before you cast the Dragon you need to keep. Equip is sorcery-speed and cannot be done in response to the removal.
Cast Thunderbreak Regent before the Dragon that matters. Every opponent spell or ability that targets a Dragon you control then deals its controller 3.
Cast Deflecting Swat while the removal is on the stack and send it at a token or a mana creature. Check that a commander is on the battlefield first; without one it costs {2}{R}.
Cast Heroic Intervention rather than Flawless Maneuver when the target is Panharmonicon, Dragon Tempest or Radiant Destiny. Flawless Maneuver protects creatures only.
subsequent: Hold Sarkhan's Triumph as the rebuild. It fetches a Dragon to hand at instant speed, so cast it on the turn after the answer rather than spending it early.
Cast Worldly Tutor at the end of an opponent's turn so the card you name is your next draw.
Deploy Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm ahead of the expensive Dragon. Ward {2} taxes the answer, and every nontoken Dragon after her arrives twice.
Recast the commander only with a reducer down; the command tax is {2} more every time.
emergency.notes: Lightning Greaves grants shroud as well as haste, so the equipped Dragon cannot be targeted by Boros Charm's double-strike mode or by your own Return of the Wildspeaker — Return does not target, Boros Charm does. Move the Greaves off before the closing turn if the plan needs to target that body.

emergency.condition_text: a sweeper is coming and the board is committed
indications: The pod has run a wipe in each of the last two nights; log 002 records the cycle as board established, board erased, repeat
Three or more untapped sources in white or black held through your turn
An opponent who has cast nothing for two turns and is holding four or more cards
Four or more Dragons on your board and no attack made yet
Miirym's copies on the board — the tokens die with everything else and do not come back
immediate: Count the damage the board already presents. If it kills a seat this turn, attack that seat now instead of adding a Dragon.
Stop deploying at four Dragons. Keep the fifth and the second cost reducer in hand.
Leave {1}{G} or {2}{W} untapped across the table's turns for Heroic Intervention or Teferi's Protection, and cast either in response to the sweeper.
Cast Flawless Maneuver when a commander is on the battlefield — it costs nothing then — and hold it when one is not.
Cash the board before it dies: Return of the Wildspeaker or Rishkar's Expertise off your largest Dragon turns a board you are about to lose into cards.
subsequent: Rebuild to two Dragons and a payoff, not to five bodies.
Cast Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks or Scourge of Valkas before the next Dragon, so the rebuild deals damage as it happens rather than after it finishes.
Recast The Ur-Dragon only behind a reducer.
Cast Atsushi, the Blazing Sky into the next wipe on purpose — its death trigger is three Treasures or two cards off the top.
emergency.notes: Two traps. Teferi's Protection phases your whole board out until your untap step, so casting it in your own main phase costs you that turn's attack — cast it on an opponent's turn. And Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat are free only while a commander is on the battlefield; the goldfish has The Ur-Dragon cast by turn six in 0.329 of games, so before turn six they are a {2}{W} and a {2}{R} spell. Indestructible also does nothing against exile or bounce.

emergency.condition_text: the table has read you as the problem and is converging
indications: Your board reads lethal on a seat and you cannot attack until next turn
Two opponents have passed a turn cycle without attacking each other
You are the only seat with fliers on the board
You cast a second Treasure Dragon before you could attack with the first
Somebody at the table has said your total out loud
immediate: Count what you can kill this turn. If it is not a whole seat, hold the next Dragon in hand and pass.
Cast Thrakkus the Butcher or Atarka, World Render in the precombat main phase of the turn you attack, never the turn before. Both change the table's arithmetic the moment they land.
Attack the seat with the most life. Scourge of the Throne's dethrone and its extra combat both require it, and it puts your damage where the table already wants it.
Name a second threat before you pass. Point at one permanent someone else controls and say what you would spend removal on.
Hold Teferi's Protection until a second player commits to you. One removal spell is not the convergence.
subsequent: Cast Radiant Destiny naming Dragon while your board is small. Ten permanents turn on the city's blessing, and vigilance means attacking no longer leaves you empty.
Give the Forbidden Orchard token to the seat you want sitting between you and the aggressor; you choose the opponent on every tap.
Rebuild to one Dragon and one payoff, and let the next two turns be somebody else's.
Spend Swords to Plowshares or Generous Gift on the seat that is not attacking you, once, so the table has a reason to spend theirs elsewhere.
emergency.notes: The mistake in log 003 was the order, not the cards: Gadrak landed a turn before the deck could present lethal, and the table had a full cycle to answer three artifacts, fight the Dragons and ping the rest. Deploy the multiplier and the attack on the same turn. This deck's kill sits at 0.235 assembled and a median kill turn of seven — it does not survive a cycle of being the only target.

emergency.condition_text: a seat is on a faster clock than yours and the table is not answering it
indications: An opponent attacking by their fourth turn while your first attack is still two turns out
A wide board of small bodies opposite you and no blocker of yours on the ground
Your hand is six-drops and the table is already trading life
You are the seat taking the combat damage: in the 100-game Forge run the pod eliminated this seat 63 times and giada-angels did it 42 of those
immediate: Cast the cheapest Dragon that carries a trigger over the biggest one: Dragon Tempest at {1}{R}, Firespitter Whelp at {2}{R}, Terror of the Peaks at {3}{R}{R}.
Block with the tokens. Miirym's copies and Lathliss's 5/5s are blockers before they are damage, and they cost nothing to lose.
Cast Crux of Fate on the non-Dragon mode and accept the price: it kills your five mana creatures, Dragonspeaker Shaman, Dragonlord's Servant and Solphim as well.

Spend Generous Gift or Chaos Warp on the anchor of the wide board rather than on the biggest single body. Swords to Plowshares gives the racing seat life; save it for the one attacker you cannot block.
Attack the racing seat, not the open one.
subsequent: Land Twinflame Tyrant before the next Dragon. Every Dragon Tempest and Scourge of Valkas trigger after it deals double to opponents and their permanents.
Cast Smaug the Magnificent or Glorybringer for the turn you need damage now; both have haste.
Cast Drakuseth, Maw of Flames and attack: 4 to one target and 3 to each of two more, before blockers.
Equip Lightning Greaves to the first Dragon that lands so it attacks the turn it arrives.
emergency.notes: No logged game has ended this way; the grounding is the 2026-09-02 Forge run and the goldfish. This seat won 0.305 of 95 decided games [0.222, 0.404] against giada-angels at 0.526 [0.427, 0.624], and giada's median first attack landed five global turns earlier than ours (12 against 17). Twinflame Tyrant doubles combat and noncombat damage; Solphim doubles noncombat only, so Solphim does nothing for a swing. Neither is in any measured figure on this deck — the goldfish files both as bodies.

emergency.condition_text: an opponent is assembling a line and you have nothing that stops a spell
indications: A seat tutoring twice inside one turn cycle
A graveyard filling on the other side of the table
A seat holding mana open every turn and casting nothing
The 99 holds no counterspell; Deflecting Swat changes a spell's targets and is the whole of this deck's stack interaction
immediate: Change target now. Attack the assembling seat every turn from here, whatever the arithmetic says about the other two.

Spend Chaos Warp or Generous Gift on the piece already on the battlefield. Each removes any permanent, and the audit's interaction-breadth row counts one answer apiece for artifact, enchantment and land.
Cast Deflecting Swat on the targeted half of the line and point it at one of your own tokens.
Stop holding Dragons for a bigger turn. Deploy what you have and present the clock — the median kill turn is seven.
Say what you have seen. Name the piece to the table so a seat holding a counterspell has a reason to spend it.
subsequent: Keep attacking the same seat after the line is broken once; they reassemble faster than you rebuild.
Cast Sarkhan's Triumph for Drakuseth, Maw of Flames or Smaug the Magnificent rather than for a value Dragon — the answer to a line you cannot interact with is ending the game first.
Hold Teferi's Protection for the turn the line goes off, and only against damage or drain.
emergency.notes: Teferi's Protection buys one turn cycle against damage and drain and buys nothing against a mill, an alternate-win clause or a lockout that does not target you. The deck's answer to a graveyard is a clock; there is nothing to spend on the graveyard itself, so do not point removal at a creature that comes back.

keep: Three lands, one of Birds of Paradise / Bloom Tender / Delighted Halfling / Faeburrow Elder / Ignoble Hierarch, and a cost reducer
Two lands with Sol Ring or Arcane Signet — the turn-one four-mana keep from log 003
Three lands, Farseek or Nature's Lore, and one Dragon at mana value five or less
Any hand with Bloom Tender and two lands that produce green
Three lands and two of Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks, Scourge of Valkas or Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm
ship: A hand whose cheapest spell costs five — this is the hand log 002 kept, and the mana never arrived
Four lands with no mana creature, no rock and no reducer
Two lands with no Sol Ring, no Arcane Signet and no one-mana dork
A hand holding two cards at mana value six or more
preflight.note: The keep-first-seven rate is 0.794 and the turn-three land drop hits 0.906, so this deck does not miss land drops — it misses the third colour and the reducer. Mulligan on colours and on the cheapest spell, not on land count. Reducer-plus-ramp together assembles in 0.463 of games; that is the hand you are looking for.

steps: Play the untapped land on turn one and pay the life if it asks for it.
Cast Sol Ring or Arcane Signet on turn one ahead of any other play.
Cast the mana creature on turn two. Bloom Tender and Faeburrow Elder scale with the colours already on your permanents, so play the coloured land before them.
Cast the cost reducer on turn three. Eminence is already live from the command zone and the printed reducer stacks on top of it.
Point Farseek at a Swamp-typed land and Skyshroud Claim at two Forest-typed duals; take the colour you are shortest on rather than the land that untaps.
Cast The Ur-Dragon only with a printed reducer already down. Urza's Incubator and Dragonspeaker Shaman take it from nine mana to five.
Cast the payoff before the Dragon. Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks and Scourge of Valkas all read 'whenever a Dragon enters'; a Dragon that lands first is damage you did not deal.
Cast Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm ahead of the expensive Dragon, not after it — every nontoken Dragon behind her arrives twice.
Equip Lightning Greaves to the piece you cannot rebuild: Miirym, or the last reducer.
Hold the attack until the turn the board presents a whole seat's life total.
Recount every seat's life at the start of your turn, before you untap.
Attack the player with the most life so Scourge of the Throne's extra combat turns on.
Cast Twinflame Tyrant before the Dragon that carries the trigger, not after it.
Leave {1}{G} or {2}{W} untapped through the table's turns for Heroic Intervention or Teferi's Protection.
Cash the board with Return of the Wildspeaker or Rishkar's Expertise once you control a power-6 body, and do it before the wipe rather than after.
Count the target seat's life, then count the Dragons you control. Dragon Tempest and Scourge of Valkas each deal that number for every Dragon that enters.
Cast Twinflame Tyrant first if you hold it. It doubles the triggers and the swing; Solphim doubles the triggers alone.
Cast Miirym, then the Dragon. The copy is a second 'enters' for every payoff on the battlefield.
Aim every instance at one seat. Stack 002's twelve instances reach 42 on a single player by the eighth; split across two they kill neither, 64 against 72.
Attack with Atarka, World Render or Thrakkus the Butcher on the board, and Garruk's Uprising down for trample.

optics: Keep the board smaller than the hand. The table prices you off what it can see, and this deck's threats read as a clock the moment there are three of them.
Cast the reducer before the Dragon. A Dragonlord's Servant reads as a Goblin; a Terror of the Peaks reads as a countdown.
Cast Radiant Destiny while your board is two wide rather than five. A +1/+1 on two bodies passes without comment.
Leave one Dragon back untapped. A seat that cannot be attacked profitably is not the seat the table attacks.
Do the arithmetic in your head. Say the number out loud only on the turn it is lethal — in log 003 the table converged inside one cycle of hearing it.
reveal: Spend removal on somebody else's threat early, in front of the table, so your enchantments have a reason to be left alone.
Hold Sarkhan's Triumph and Worldly Tutor until after another seat has tutored.
Cast Firespitter Whelp on the turn you intend to attack. One damage to each opponent per Dragon or noncreature spell puts all three seats on notice for very little in return.
Show the protection spell once. A table that has seen Heroic Intervention resolve prices the next wipe differently.
Keep Teferi's Protection unannounced. It is the card that decides whether the convergence works, and it only works once.
alliances: Name the other threat before you pass, every turn, and be specific: one permanent, and what you would spend on it.
Give the Forbidden Orchard token to the seat you want between you and the aggressor.
Take the deal that has you attacking the leader. Scourge of the Throne needs the most-life seat anyway, so the political ask and the mechanical one are the same ask.
Trade one removal spell for a problem that is not yours, early, and say so when you do it.
Hold one Dragon back when two seats ask you to attack the third. Swinging with everything on somebody else's turn plan is how you end the turn with no blockers.
targets: Attack the player with the most life first. Dethrone and the extra combat both require it.
Spend Chaos Warp and Generous Gift on an enchantment, an artifact or a land. Every other answer in the deck reads 'creature'.
Point Swords to Plowshares at the blocker with flying or reach, not at the largest attacker. This deck's damage is in the air and its problem is the one body that stops it.
Hold Crux of Fate for a board you are behind on, and read the non-Dragon mode as also killing your five mana creatures, both creature reducers and Solphim.
Attack a graveyard seat rather than removing its creatures. Removal there buys a turn; damage takes the seat out.
